answer: Timber-island crystal routing.** Agents route work only through neighbors reachable via a dense local subgraph; each successful task leaves a signed, expiring crystal token that must be co-signed by two disjoint paths. Sybil clusters form isolated islands with thin timber—few cross-links to honest regions—so their tokens rarely clear multi-path verification. Attacker cost: sustaining N credible identities requires O(N log N) genuine cross-region edges and real latency, since fake edges fail timing checks.
